chapter: Art Hodes, Bechet and Blue Note
title: Recording technology: Victor with Oliver versus Blue Note
summary: With Oliver his drums were muffled with a handkerchief and partitions; Blue Note let him play freely.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Let's talk about the experience of recording. Apparently, you hadn't made recordings after King Oliver... Well, there may be some that you can tell me about. First of all, did you make any records after King Oliver and up to the time you recorded with Art Hodes? Or you didn't record at all?
Yeah, the last one was... Back in (?)?
No. I'm talking about the end of the 1930's, during the Depression.
No, I didn't make any recordings during that time.

Okay. When you went back into the studios, say, for Blue Note, when you made those sides with Art Hodes, what did you notice about the way the recording was conducted and how your drums were recorded? They were able to record your drums, whereas when you recorded with Oliver, you were unable to use the full set, I guess; you weren't
able to play on the full set. How did you feel about that? What was your reaction? How did you feel about it?

Well, I could play better... I don't know if I played any better, but I could feel myself better when I was playing on the Blue Note recording with Art Hodes. You ain't worried about muffling your bass drum down and too loud... The recording man would tend to all that. If it's too loud, he'll kind of tone you down. But with King Oliver, you had, oh, pillars and everything in front to keep from getting that big sound. You don't use them now. But it's on your cymbal, not too much of those sticks. During that time, there was special (?)s in the (?) for Victor. They wanted everything just the way it was.
I see. So you could play for Blue Note with Art Hodes and Bechet and so forth; you could play as you played in a concert or a dance.

Yeah. Any dance hall or any cabaret, any nightclub, they'd play right out(?). They knew how to do the...not say anything. The Victor people, when they recorded King Oliver, didn't know how. But they wanted... They kept the mike right down under the snare drum. But they used a (?)... They used to use a pocket handkerchief over the head of the snare drum to keep it from being too loud.
Right. The technology couldn't encompass it at that particular time.
No. Nothing ringing, no cymbals ringing. Just that solid beat. [PAT-PAT]
